newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air cargo agents need overseas links to be viable.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo agents need overseas links to be viable.

text.p: Air cargo agents with poor international links could go out of business as larger forwarders seize more market share, a leading German forwarder warned.
Wolf-Dietrich von Helldorff, air cargo committee chairman of German forwarders association BSL and German airfreight director of Kuehne & Nagel, forecast market concentration would gather pace.

"We are already speaking about a very centralised market. I believe the market will split between global players with a worldwide network who will be the strongest economically," he said in a BSL briefing.
The top ten international forwarders already accounted for 30 percent of the market by volume while the top ten freight airlines controlled 60 percent of total market weight.
"I still see a strong existence far the small forwarder, the specialists with personal connections to shippers who have no problems to keep costs low," von Helldorff noted.
The biggest problem will be for the medium-sized forwarders with no international network but with higher costs to cover. They are the candidates to go," he forecast.
Von Helldorff declined to estimate how many of Germany's 215 accredited IATA air cargo forwarders in might disappear from the market in the near future.
